messages:
incident-bot: PAGE TRIGGERED — sev2 GPU OOMs on decode/stream fleet (node flapping)
incident-bot: fingerprint: gpu.decode.stream.oom | affected_pools: decode-stream-prod-* | svc: inference-runtime | started: 2026-03-15T09:04:16Z
sarah: I'm on it — seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on two nodes in cluster decode-stream-prod-us-west-2-03. Streaming requests drop mid-response. Root logs: `CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.04 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 14.02 GiB already allocated)`
alex: confirm — metrics spike on p99 token latency and a rise in 500s from the streaming endpoint around 09:03-09:05 UTC.
mike: any recent config change to max_tokens or streaming buffer?
sarah: not at infra level. We had a rollout earlier to increase max_tokens default from 1024 -> 8192 for a canary tenant last night, but it was scoped. Suspect runaway generation from malformed prompt in production traffic + KV cache behavior causing big KV growth.
lia: looking at tracing — the requests that fail have sustained decode loops (tokens generated >> requested). We see client-sent max_tokens ignored on a small fraction where the middleware failed to attach policy.
jordan: paging infra oncall to check node flaps and autoscaler behavior — @ops-bot can you pull node event logs and node GPU memory utilization for the last 10m?
ops-bot: run: `rictl nodes events --since 10m --pool decode-stream-prod-us-west-2-03`
ops-bot: returned 8 events: 3 container restarts, 2 cuda-driver errors, 3 scheduler preemptions.
sarah: mitigation plan: 1) apply emergency request-level max_tokens override for streaming endpoint to 256 for 10m, 2) set per-request reject for >64k token KV growth, 3) route traffic to fallback pool (decode-stream-prod-us-west-2-01) with smaller models, 4) cordon + restart the two flapping nodes.
alex: commands: 
```
# override policy for streaming route
rictl routes update --route streaming.v1 --policy 'max_tokens=256, reject_on_kv_growth=true' --dur 10m
# fallback routing
rictl routes set-fallback --route streaming.v1 --target decode-stream-prod-us-west-2-01
```
mike: can we do a hotfix to inject a guard in the middleware to enforce client max_tokens? quick patch?
sarah: we can deploy a lightweight rejector (Lua filter) via edge config in ~6-8 minutes. Doing that now.
lia: I'm validating which customers' requests hit the failing nodes — looks like two high-throughput customers (cust-alpha, cust-bravo) were heavy. We'll notify support.
jordan: I'm taking over oncall in 26m. Will watch the reroute and node cordon. sarah, handoff when you start restart.
sarah: starting emergency config now. Applying override.
sarah: `rictl routes update ...` returned OK. Edge config deploying.
ops-bot: deployment ok: edge filter active on streaming.v1; matched and rejected 1.8k requests in 30s (client attempted runaway generation)
alex: metrics: token growth trending down. Node GPU mem pressure on the two nodes declined from 95%->38% after reroute. 500s rate decreased to baseline.
lia: customer impact: estimated 1.7% of streaming sessions experienced mid-stream drop between 09:03-09:11 UTC. We have 3 support tickets open from cust-alpha reporting interrupted transcripts. No SLA breach yet but we flagged potential tail latency SLO risk.
mike: cuda-driver errors — do we need drivers bumped?
ops-bot: logs from node decode-stream-prod-us-west-2-03:
```
[09:03:42Z] runtime: CudaCheckFailure: cuCtxSynchronize() -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[09:03:43Z] container: pid=2245 restart -> exit code 137
[09:04:01Z] kernel: mlx5_core: device reset triggered
```
sarah: cordoning node and draining: `rictl node cordon decode-stream-prod-us-west-2-03 && rictl node drain --grace 30s --force`
jordan: I see the cordon in progress. Starting controlled restarts of inference containers on flapping nodes.
sarah: restarted the container runtime on node 03 and cleared driver caches per KB procedure. Node 03 rejoined and memory back to normal.
alex: monitoring shows another small OOM on node 05 (different rack) at 09:24. It looks like a follow-up where a poorly formed customer session hit increased max_tokens.
lia: next steps: 1) keep emergency override for 30m, 2) leave fallback routing in place for 1h, 3) create a temporary alert to fire if per-node OOMs > 1 within 15m, 4) open a postmortem.
mike: recommend we add a hard safety net in runtime: absolute token cap at kernel level to prevent runaway loops irrespective of config. I'll draft a PR.
jordan: taking over fully for monitoring. sarah — great work, handing off. I'll coordinate with support for customer comms and with platform for the postmortem.
sarah: handing off — notes added to the incident doc: `incident/1779123456` with log extracts and commands run.
lia: support notif: cust-alpha & cust-bravo contacted, incident severity set to advisory, suggested temporary retry/backoff in client.
jordan: updating timeline and will schedule a blameless postmortem. Assign owners: mike -> runtime safety net PR, alex -> metrics/alerts tune, lia -> customer comms and support follow-up.
sarah: closing immediate page — watch for any new OOMs; please escalate to pager if p95 token latency or 5xx rate goes above threshold. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
jordan: note for handoff: if recurrence, next action is to scale dedicated pool by +2 GPUs and force-run model quantization profile on fallback nodes.
mike: will open PR for kernel cap and include integration tests simulating runaway decode.
lia: will compile customer-facing summary and send to #support after postmortem draft.
incident-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: id=INC-2026-0315-1779123456 | status=monitoring | severity=sev2 | assignees=[jordan,mike,lia]
